text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White) FM reception is flat out horrible where I live. It's like a radeo dead zone. My home theater system can pull in nothing. My stereo gets a lot of static. I listen almost exclusively online but I'd heard good things about this radio so I decided to give it a try. The reception was amazing. Perfectly clear. No static on FM at all. It sounds beautiful. The weather feed was full of static, but servicable--I ususally can't pull in the weather band at all. AM is average--neither the worse I've heard nor the best. But then, I don't expect much from AM.

It does the FM1, FM2 trick that some cars do. There is no difference. It just lets them repurpose the buttons. I find it odd, but not bad.

The only think I would have changed is how it hangs. If you don't have a shower hook (I don't) it hangs over the shower head. That tilts the entire unit forward. It should either suspend from the shower curtain rack (the strap is oriented the wrong way to do that--it would try to hand perpendicular to the curtain) or reach a better balance point. That's an issue of aesthetics, not function. I'd be worried about sitting it on the edge of the tub, as it is too likely to fall.

The one trick to remember, when sticking the antenna to the shower wall, is that suction cups don't work as well on a wet surface. Thoroughly dry the wall first, then place it. It helps will the issue of the antenna falling.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White)

text_fidelity_a:
Apple AirPods Max Wireless Over-Ear Headphones. Active Noise Cancelling, Transparency Mode, Spatial Audio, Digital Crown for Volume Control. Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone - Green I see people raving up and down about the perfection and wonderfulness of these headphones; I’m not as completely blown away by them as those people are. Quality of construction does seem to be excellent (although because Amazon doesn’t lower all prices at the start of Prime Day but only lowers some of them well after Prime Day has begun, I had to send back the first pair I bought and purchase another pair to get a discounted price, and the piston things for extending and compressing the size of the headphones was smoother on the first pair I had) and they’re comfortable enough to wear for extended periods, but while it may be a limitation of Bluetooth (I don’t know), I haven’t noticed myself being amazed by their bass response. No, in fact I just now watched the video for Shake It Off and listened to a couple of Lana Del Rey tracks and these headphones are definitely lacking in bass response – as in, there’s very little, and what there is gets completely lost under any midrange and high-end sounds that may be playing at the same time. They’re tinny-sounding. I have to wonder what the people are listening to with these who are praising the sound quality so enthusiastically.

On the other hand, I don’t ordinarily listen to music anymore, but only to talks and lectures; While I’m watching movies is probably the only time I’m going to really want big bass, and I watched The Revenant last night and didn’t feel like I was missing anything…

So their construction is much more solid than that of probably most other headphones on the market, they’re comfortable to wear, and there’s a nice ecosystem of accessories out there, but I personally find the sound quality quite lacking and I’m going to have to decide whether to hang onto these or return them.
text_fidelity_b: Apple AirPods Max Wireless Over-Ear Headphones. Active Noise Cancelling, Transparency Mode, Spatial Audio, Digital Crown for Volume Control. Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone - Green

Winegard FL5500A FlatWave Amped Digital HD Indoor Amplified TV Antenna (4K Ready / ATSC 3.0 Ready / High-VHF / UHF), 60 Mile Long Range, Black/White, 6 Feet I am absolutely thrilled with the performance of this antenna. I was using a Antenna Direct antenna which worked sort of OK, but had problems pulling in some stations and was rather bulky. This FlatWave is a major improvement. I'm picking up nearly twice as many channels -- all of which are clear -- and the form factor makes this hardly noticeable in the room.

It is a powered antenna, and can draw power either from a wall outlet (using the included transformer) or via a USB cable plugged into the TV (or anything else that can power a USB device). Installation is very easy -- just plug it into the TV, power source, and you're done.

The antenna itself is a flat sheet of plastic about the thickness of a thin piece of cardboard. I have mine mounted in the window which works great. Positioning is critical -- you'll want to try out a few different positions for the antenna to see which works best for your coverage area.

Absolutely zero complaints. It's simple to use, works great, and is very easy to hide. Highly recommend.

Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th] My title pretty much sums it up - I love the Kindle Paperwhite! I am a big reader, but I resisted the e-reader obsession until December 2010 when I gave into a Nook. Back then I decided on a Nook because the Kindle did not allow you to borrow books from the library, which was a deal breaker for me.

Fast-forward two and a half years... My Nook was getting older and the discrepancy between prices and availability of e-books between Amazon and Barnes & Noble was becoming increasingly clearer. Also, I love Amazon as a general rule, and order from them pretty heavily for a variety of items, so it made sense to switch over. After brief research, I stumbled upon the Kindle Paperwhite. It met all of my requirements - a dedicated e-reader (no tablet for me, thanks), with a built in light. Yippee! My hubby and puppy (okay, just the hubby) purchased the Kindle Paperwhite for my birthday at the end of August and it was love at first sight. It is unreasonable to compare the Kindle Paperwhite to my old Nook, so I won't. I can freely admit that most of my love comes from the new technology and association with Amazon. I love the light. It is awesome to not have to use a clip on light at night. They are usually terrible and not evenly spaced. The light makes reading at night a breeze. Plus, it is a perfect light, so it really is like reading a book and not like reading on a backlit screen (a la the iPhone or iPad). I love the ease of purchasing books from Amazon, and I love their prices and special deals. But, most of all, I love checking out library books! The very thing that turned me away from the Kindle initially is now the best. There is no need to connect my Kindle to a laptop to download a book. Yay! I can just wirelessly send a book to my Kindle, the same as purchasing one. You must be a wireless network (not 3G), but that my dear friends is a tiny issue. Overall, I love my Kindle Paperwhite and I cannot think of one single thing to make it better! Love it.

Helpful tips - 3G or not? I love the 3G, but it's not a necessity if you have wide access to wireless. I would definitely say to go for the ads, however. They are entirely inoffensive and unobtrusive. They only come up when your Kindle is asleep. Save the $20 and buy yourself a few books!

text_fidelity_a:
TV Antenna - 1byone Amplified 50 Mile HDTV Digital Antenna Powerful Amplifier Signal Booster for All TV 4K UHF VHF 1080P Local Channels with 20ft Coaxial Cable This is a review of the 50 mile OUS00-0562 model. To summarize: It works. But it's no better than my cheap [[ASIN:B000HKGK8Y RCA Indoor FM and HDTV Antenna]] antenna that I was trying to replace, yet costing several times more.

With my cheap RCA "rabbit ears" antenna I was getting 18 channels, being 8 miles away from the transmitter. According to my digital-to-analog converter most TV signals were in the range of 75% to 30%. I was looking for a better antenna to improve the signal quality, so when I saw that the OUS00-0562 model was on sale I bought it. I didn't believe the 50 mile claim of this antenna since most antennas with this claim are large, more expensive and rather directional. But I figured that even if it was half that it had to be better than my RCA one. Whatever this antenna was directional of not was not specified, I assumed that it was not.

The OUS00-0562 model comes with an antenna with a 20 foot non-removable cord. This was disappointing, but I should have realized this when looking at the product pictures. Having so much cable slack is a waste when it sits 3 feet from the TV. Before I installed the 1byone antenna I took note of signal strength of each channel of my RCA antenna. The OUS00-0562 package also comes with an amplifier, which I connected to my RCA antenna as a test - and was disappointed. Only 3 channels were 10% higher, and that was within margin of error. The OUS00-0562 disappointed me soon after, as there was no change in signal strength on any channel over the RCA antenna (except that it gave me two more channels at 40% signal).

The short version:

RCA "rabbit ears" - 18 channels, 75%-30% (+/- 5%)
RCA "rabbit ears" with 1byone amplifier - 18 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)
1byone OUS00-0562 with 1byone amplifier - 20 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)

I tried to reposition the OUS00-0562 antenna to see if there was a directional issue, if I was out of the "sweat spot." I did notice 5-10% dips here and there but no marked improvements. I didn't spend much time on this and since it wasn't shipped with a stand. You can buy one, but I didn't want to spend any more money on it since to me it was overpriced as is. I promptly returned it.

I will give this antenna one point though. It's better looking than the RCA antenna and it takes up less space. So if looks and space matter, it might be for you.
text_fidelity_b: TV Antenna - 1byone Amplified 50 Mile HDTV Digital Antenna Powerful Amplifier Signal Booster for All TV 4K UHF VHF 1080P Local Channels with 20ft Coaxial Cable

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin vívoactive HR GPS Smart Watch, Regular fit - Black I really like this GPS sports watch so far. Garmin makes a huge range of sports watches. This vivoactive HR is one of their lower priced GPS watches. It doesn't have the more advanced sports training features or build quality of the more expensive Garmin Fenix and Forerunner watches. However, for this price, you do get GPS and smartwatch features in addition to basic fitness tracking.

I tried the GPS mode on a 3-hour bike ride, running my dedicated bicycle computer at the same time. Distance calculations of the 2 units were less than 1 mile different, which I think is very good for small portable units like this. Current speed was always about the same, though looking at the watch to see your speed while riding is kind of difficult, especially compared to the big display on my handlebar-mounted bike computer. You can mount the watch on your bicycle handlebar, but that would of course disable the heart rate tracking feature of the watch. The wrist-based heart rate monitor is not as accurate as a chest-strap heart rate monitor, with a slower response time that is very apparent during interval training (short bursts of high-intensity effort), but you can connect an ANT+ HR monitor to this watch to improve accuracy.

GPS mode has an advertised battery life of 16 hours, which I think is really terrific for a gadget of this size. My 3 hour bike ride burned about 20% of the battery on the vivo, so 16 hours of GPS time is plausible. Garmin also advertises 8 days of battery life with the GPS turned off, but realistically, who buys a $250 GPS watch and never turns on the GPS? Still, I expect to get in at least a couple of long bike rides or several runs before having to recharge this watch. Recharging is very quick using the USB charging cradle included with the watch. Because battery life is so good, you don't need a spare charger for your office like you might need with the Apple smartwatch.

If you have a (free) Garmin account, you can upload your daily activity to the Garmin server so you can review it on their website afterwards. This is useful for tracking your fitness progress (speed, distance, etc) over time.

The smartwatch features are pretty basic (compared to dedicated smartwatches from Apple or Google), showing phone call caller-ID and copying notifications from your smartphone (via Bluetooth) and displaying them on the watch. If you like checking your notifications quickly and don't want to pull your phone out every time it beeps, getting them on your watch is great. If I'm jogging or in a business meeting or at dinner but am expecting an important message, I can just glance at the watch and quickly ignore it if it isn't important. I have my notifications for high-priority emails, SMS, and a couple of messaging apps synced with my phone. This seems to work mostly flawlessly with my Samsung smartphone. Occasionally, the notifications will stop working but restarting my phone fixes that. I don't know if that is a problem with the phone's base software or with the Garmin app that runs on my phone. The Garmin app that runs on your smartphone lets you pick which app's notifications to show on the watch. I do not know how this works with Apple phones. There are some other smartwatch apps like weather forecasts and calendar, but I'm not sure if scrolling through these on your small watch face is really easier than pulling out your phone to view the app on the larger screen there.

If you're comparing this Garmin watch to an Apple smartwatch, yes Apple has a lot more apps, but Garmin has an 8 day battery life compared to less than 1 day for Apple. Personally, battery life is more valuable to me since there are not yet any killer apps for the Apple watch. Having a dead watch because you forgot to charge it the night before is not fun. Also, the Garmin watch has a built-in GPS, while the Apple watch does not. This means you can record a bike ride or run carrying only the watch, not your phone as well.

Garmin also has basic fitness tracking features like resting heart rate, sleep tracking, intensive exercise tracking, step counting, etc. If you're active enough to want to spend money a GPS sports watch (instead of a cheap fitness band), I don't think the step counting is going to be interesting to you. I bike or run at least 10 hours every week of the year and steps have no interest to me. Resting heart rate is an indicator of your health and fitness and I'm looking forward to tracking that. Intensive exercise tracking may also be useful if you tend to slack off during your exercise. Sleep tracking is reportedly not too accurate on this watch (it can't tell if you're really sleeping or reading a book in bed), but that isn't something that greatly interests me.

On the subjective side, this chunky plastic rectangular watch does look like a fitness tracker rather than a real watch. The much better looking Garmin Fenix looks like something you could wear to the office, but this watch maybe not. At least the vivoactive has a very comfortable wristband that should fit well on a range of wrist sizes.

Again, this is one of Garmin's cheaper GPS watches. I think the features and performance are great for this price point, but if you're involved in hard core training program, you should definitely look at the features of some of Garmin's better GPS watches.

I would have given this watch 5 stars for functionality and value for the price if it was better looking, but Garmin seems to have made it intentionally ugly in try to upsell you on their better looking and more expensive Fenix and Forerunner watches.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin vívoactive HR GPS Smart Watch, Regular fit - Black

text_fidelity_a:
CanaKit Raspberry Pi 3 Complete Starter Kit - 32 GB Edition This is a very complete kit and does contain everything you need to setup a Raspberry Pi 3. Yes, the op system installs easily and, with luck, you can be up and running in less than an hour. So, why the 2 stars?

It gets 2 stars because the Raspberry Pi is probably one of the most frustrating devices I've ever tried to put to any real use. For example, I wanted to set it up so I could use a VNC server on the Pi and a VNC client on my Mac (OS X El Capitan). After three days of almost non-stop failures, I'm sick of this thing. Researching how to get this task done leads you down a black hole of internet articles and posts on the Raspberry Pi site, most of that give different instructions, use different commands, tell you which files to edit and what to put in them, and almost none work, period!

The core problem rests squarely on the Raspberry Pi organization. Their own website is full of conflicting posts on how to do just about anything beyond a basic setup. Few, if any posts state which model of Pi is being referenced, and many bear no date. All in all, it's a very frustrating experience and, while I like to tinker with these things, a little success is required once in a while to keep me chugging along. I think I'm done with this thing. I had hoped it would finally be a Linux for the rest of us. Unfortunately, it's just as convoluted and difficult to use as any version of Linux out there (my opinion).

However, if you're looking to explore the Pi, this kit has everything you need to do a basic setup of Linux. And, should you want to use it as a web server, file server, media server, you're really on your own. Drink lots of coffee and plan to pull our lots of hair.
text_fidelity_b: CanaKit Raspberry Pi 3 Complete Starter Kit - 32 GB Edition

text_fidelity_a: WYZE Cam 1080p HD Indoor Smart Home Camera with Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Compatible with Alexa & the Google Assistant Bulbs and outlet are OK. I would not buy separately though, as nowadays you get higher quality bulbs and outlets for a discount price.  The sensor bridge, contact and motion sensors are problematic to say the least. I have 2 contact sensors and 3 motion sensors connected to the sensor bridge. Right now all of them are offline, they started going offline one by one. Distance from the sensors to the bridge is not an issue since two of them are located no more than three feet away from the bridge. This is not the first time this has happened. The only solution for me has been to reset bridge and sensors, and reinstall them one by one. Many people complain about the same issue, and this keeps happening. The camera where the bridge is attached is installed 7 ft from the ground, so it has been very aggravating to have to get a ladder every time one of these switches has gone offline. Regarding the camera, you probably will not find anything cheaper in the market right now. This model in particular offers continuous recording provided you insert a storage card, that is a plus. Person detection is back, however sometimes it takes more than 10 minutes to receive a notification. Some people has reported that it has take up to one hour to get the notification. I personally would not recommend getting this package due to the unreliability of the bridge and motion and contact sensors. This is definitely not a system you want to buy to secure your home. The camera can be purchased separately for about $25. The video quality is acceptable during the daytime. If you want a hobby camera, you will not find a better deal. For security purposes, you are better off looking somewhere else.

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF-S 10-18mm f/4.5-5.6 is STM Lens, Lens Only I really bought a Canon DSLR (vs Nikon, or any of the mirrorless Cameras) for this lens. I needed a low distortion very wide lens for real estate videos and I also needed image stabilization and quiet focusing. I don't think there is any other lens from any manufacturer that satisfies all of those things except this one. (Sigma has the 10-20mm but no stabilization, lower optical quality, and more money! Tamaron - 10-24 - same story. And so on ).
GOOD: Excellent optical quality for the price. This lens is noticeably sharper and has less distortion at 10mm than my kit lens 18-135mm has at 18mm. Stabilization works very well. Focusing is very fast and silent. I don't hear it even with the built in mic when shooting video (on a Canon 70D). Extremely lightweight and fairly compact.

BAD: Maximum Aperture. This is NOT a fast lens. F/4.5 maximum is not that great and you lose it pretty quickly as you zoom in since the max aperture ranges from 4.5 - 5.6. You need to have some decent light to shoot with this lens. But given the lack of competition in super wide stabilized silent EF-S lenses (or any Canon mount lens) and the price of anything vaguely similar, I think it's a reasonable compromise.

Note: At this price, you can't really call it a knock, but it'd be nice if it came with the lens hood. You can get a clone lens hood for $10 or so.

ALSO: Canon has now updated their EOS Utility software for this lens.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 10-18mm f/4.5-5.6 is STM Lens, Lens Only

Kensington Pro Fit® Ergo Vertical Wireless Trackball (K75326WW), Black, 3" x 4" x 6.1" Initially, I liked the ergonomic design. It put much less pressure on my wrist than the Logitech trackball I've been using for many years. Unfortunately, when I started up World of Warcraft, I noticed the Kensington trackball button mapping software disabled the ability to use more than one button at once. I found the same detriment in Overwatch where multiple buttons often need to be pressed simultaneously. When I contacted the company, they sent me an email. The following is a direct quote from their email:
"Thank you for contacting Kensington Technical Support.

We would like to inform you that these trackballs are designed for basic office use and will not work on gaming applications.

We appreciate your time and patience."

To me, this came across as rather rude. This, coupled with the fact that this very mouse shows up in searches for gaming trackball mouse made me extremely disappointed and, in fact, somewhat angry. I feel Kensington needs to do any or all of the following. 1. Fix the software to make their hardware gaming inclusive. 2. Stop advertising their non-gaming devices as gaming devices (I feel this is blatant false advertising.) 3. Ask customers how they could fix issues rather than giving them a short, curt email to inform us that we, apparently, are idiots for expecting their devices to work as advertised.

Bottom line: I do not recommend buying this product unless all you intend to use it for is emails and youtube.
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Pro Fit® Ergo Vertical Wireless Trackball (K75326WW), Black, 3" x 4" x 6.1"

It also does a setup for having the remote control the TV and the receiver (my Fire Stick is plugged into my AV receiver). The overall speed and responsiveness is improved over earlier Fire sticks. Menus are more snappy and apps load faster. There are also a number of new settings to control audio and video aspects. I left most on their default, but it's nice to be able to get into the settings and tweak them.

***UPDATE***: While it was past the Amazon return date, it was within the OEM 1yr warranty, so I sent it back and they replaced it. I had to pay shipping to them and round trip was 2 to 3 weeks without a radio. In general I do like the unit for the money, so long as this one isn't a dud.

Installation wasn't bad. I didn't need a trim kit as the one it came with was fine. I purchased a wire harness for my Nissan Frontier and crimp connectors made the connections easy. text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W) This is an updated version of a mesh system router and satellite I already have. The technology is great when it's working, but, for whatever reason, my system has needed to be reset once a week or more, and the coverage is nowhere near as good as it claims it should be.

My hope was that the newer version would be faster and have better coverage. It isn't. It doesn't. And, like the earlier version, it has to be in AP mode to work with my FIOS modem (FIOS has a version of this available with its own firmware, but you have to buy a new one, and it won't work with any other ISP). Those hopes dashed, my next hope was that I could at least use the router as a satellite on my existing system, which, of course not.

So, you would think I could at LEAST use the satellite from the new one with the old system or the old satellite with the new one? They are the same model, after all. And that, too, would be a nope.

What I finally did, after hours on the internet (and other hours just trying to set up the new one by itself - it was the same with the old one - it for some reason despises custom settings and will not save them the first many times. It will also lose them after firmware upgrades, I expect, like its predecessor), was set it up alongside the old one with its own network name. Now I have one network serving one side of the house and the other serving the other. Speeds are good. So far, no routing issues, and I don't really expect any. The two network solution seems to have worked well for others.

But really.

If you are looking to expand your Orbi network, check out the nighthawk mesh expanders. I have the 7500, and it's excellent. Also, don't take my lukewarm review for a no-rec. The Orbi is, as far as I can tell from personal experience, buggy and locked down, but, again from personal experience, it beats the Velop (its nearest competitor) by a mile for coverage.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W)

It takes too long for the cameras to wake up so I get a lot of 'blank' clips, where whatever finally triggered the camera is over by the time it gets around to recording it. Worst of all, the whole system has a tendency to randomly go offline where it stops communicating with the cameras and nothing gets recorded. text_fidelity_a:
iParaAiluRy Soft Replacement Earpads Ear Pads Cushions for Logitech G35 G430 G930 F450 Headphones (1 Pair) My old G930 ear pads were flaking like crazy after several years of daily, all-day use, and I was hesitant to buy these at first because several people said they were too small. But I figured it's only $5, so it's worth a shot.

They arrived this morning and all I can think of is that whoever thought these were too tight or too small wasn't putting them on correctly. Maybe they thought they were just push-on instead of realizing that they have a flap (just like the ones that come with the headset) that needs to be lifted to go over the plastic part of the earpiece. That's what actually holds these things in place, people - otherwise they'd just fall off! Or maybe people aren't actually matching up the shape correctly. Either way - if you install them CORRECTLY, they fit perfectly.

These things are the correct size and I took some photos to compare the old Logitech-made pads with these. I also measured separately and they are the exact same size. If you take the time to look at how the original ear pads come off, you'll know exactly how to put these replacements on, and it'll take you all of about 10-15 seconds per ear pad.

These are virtually indistinguishable from the originals. I put these on and at first they seemed a little firmer than the original ear pads. However, I actually have a total of three G930 headsets (different purposes), so I was able to compare the feel of these ear pads to the original ear pads on one of the lesser-used, newer headsets. Again, pretty much identical - I guess they just get softer with use. Still, they are very comfortable even in their brand-new state, and I'm happy not to finish the day with black flakes on the sides of my face again.

PHOTOS:
I have three photos, two that are just comparing the back and front of the old pad to the replacement pad (and showing where the flap is that some people are apparently missing). The third photo is just showing the headset with one pad replaced so you can actually see that it looks pretty much the same as the original when installed correctly on the headset.
text_fidelity_b: iParaAiluRy Soft Replacement Earpads Ear Pads Cushions for Logitech G35 G430 G930 F450 Headphones (1 Pair)

Cat 6 Ethernet Cable 5ft (6 Pack) (at a Cat5e Price but Higher Bandwidth) Flat Internet Network Cables - Cat6 Ethernet Patch Cable Short - Black Computer LAN Cable with Snagless RJ45 Connectors And also, no mess.

I have a bunch of smart devices that use a bunch of hubs.

I don't know why it should be true, but the devices that use wired hubs are the most reliable at staying connected - Hue, SmartThings/Samsung, Aeotec - they chug right along, running their routines. They're only ever a problem when it's time to reset them, and then you need John Titor level ancient devices to get deep into your 2.4gHz network without making an executive decision to jump to 5 gHz during set up, but that's another story for another day).

Anyway - the devices that use wired hubs work better and more reliably. So I have a bunch of hubs connected to my router. The router has to be out in the great wide open. Otherwise, it does not route. It has what's supposed to be an attractive design, right? Yeah, when it's got a bunch of different colored cables sticking out of it, not so much. It looks like I used to look taking my kid to school drop off.

Flat black cables run smoothly and nearly invisibly against the black cabinet the router sits on. There's plenty of bandwidth, and the hubs don't have to be noticeable to work.

Negative space for the win.
text_fidelity_b: Cat 6 Ethernet Cable 5ft (6 Pack) (at a Cat5e Price but Higher Bandwidth) Flat Internet Network Cables - Cat6 Ethernet Patch Cable Short - Black Computer LAN Cable with Snagless RJ45 Connectors

So, I am using this in a G12 Canon Powershot (which is also shorting out on me).

HOW THIS COMES
This comes on a card.

WHY I GOT THIS
I originally got this, hoping maybe my storage card was causing the problems with my cameras, but it was not the problem.

PERFORMANCE
Although my camera was not ultra high end, it would have been good to test this with. For now, it performs very well in my older camera so far. I am waiting to be able to replace my failed camera so I can test the video aspect of this card with it.

As far as photos go, this takes great photos and even on the higher speed continuous shots it seems to work well. Then again, this is not a new camera, so that is not really saying much as this card was designed for ultra video shooting and DSLR cameras.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Since my camera quit, I have only been able to test this on older cameras. It works fine, but I have not got anything better to test it on right now.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am pretty frustrated at my cameras breaking down right now, but this will work as a good huge storage for photos for now on my older one. I hope to get a new one in the not too distant future. If I can get a friend to test this on his video camera, I will update.

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy NX EK-GN120ZKAXAR Galaxy Wireless Smart Android 4G Camera 20.3MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 4.8-Inch LCD with 18-55mm OIS Lens (Black) My first impression upon unboxing this camera was "Wow, that feels cheap." Everything's made from unattractive plastic. The single dial on the top rear of the camera (oddly blank) feels light, spins too easily and clicking it feels mushy. The other buttons on the camera, power, movie and flash all have the same, cheap, mushy feel. The shutter button has poor tactile feel.

The camera is surprisingly heavy; for me uncomfortably, painfully, so.The back is so taken up by the huge 4.8" LCD screen that the thumb rest is too short, more of an afterthought that cause me quite a bit of discomfort during extended use. The DSLR style handgrip is quite large (perhaps too large for small hands) to accommodate the massive 4360 mAh battery.

On paper the idea of an Android OS with a 4.8" LCD screen and a big APS-C sensor sounds great but I was sadly less than impressed.

Because of the Android OS startup time from fully off to ready to shoot is a very long 23 seconds. In standby mode the camera was ready to shoot in approx. 4 seconds. The camera runs warm, very warm, even just sitting idle on a cool 50 degree day. I would worry about overheating in the summer months.

Image quality was unimpressive especially in low light. Early morning, post sunrise, images with sky and clouds were extremely grainy and noisy. Performance in full light was better but not spectacular. Auto focus was run of the mill, often seeking excessively in low light situations. High ISO performance was exceedingly poor. Past ISO 800 images were rather noisier and grainy. In auto mode the camera seemed to make poor choices for ISO and shutter speeds.

Controls. Almost every setting is accessed via the large LCD screen.

There are over twenty pre-configured shooting modes. I used several of them while checking out this camera. These selections are made from a top to bottom scrolling 'carousel' where you scroll through until you find the option you want. I found it annoying to find and stop on the mode I wanted. You're going to miss shots trying to find the mode you want.

Continuous Shooting: burst mode. Surprisingly fast.
Kids Shot: the camera plays one of three sounds to attract a child's attention and then bursts five photos.
Macro: The Galaxy NX has a surprisingly short minimum focal distance with the kit lens and the macro photos I took were among the best results I was able to get from the camera.
Rich Tone: Samsung's HDR mode. Processing time was excessive.
Panorama: This is a sweep mode, smoothly move the camera (a tripod helps) to capture up to 180°'s of view. Disappointingly the camera reduces the image size significantly in Panorama mode.
Multi Exposure: combines two or more images into one.
Drama: combines several images of a moving subject into a single image. The camera was very picky about detecting moving objects. I encountered at least a 50% fail rate trying this mode. Additionally, as with the Panorama mode the image size is greatly reduced.

The camera can also be used in manual mode. Samsung calls it 'Expert Mode'. This gives you access to the standard PASM controls. The settings are controlled by three half-circle on screen dials that I found frustratingly hard to use. Try to change one and my thick fingers would spin the wrong dial. Using Shutter Priority mode I found the processing time of 30 second exposures was a disappointing additional 30 seconds.

There are some things I did like about this camera. It's not all bad. It can produce decent images and I honestly think the majority of the limitations I experienced were due to the cheap kit lens. The 4.8" LCD is gorgeous, in the right light, I recently went back to a camera with a beautiful 3" screen and it felt small. Some of the included shooting modes are fun to play with. Connectivity via WiFi was rock solid (I wasn't able to test the 3G/4G connectivity) even in parking lots of places that offered free WiFi. There were eleven gigs of free space in internal memory. That was plenty of room for a day's shooting and testing. I never did get around to installing an SD card.

In conclusion...
I'm not really sure who this camera is aimed at. They seem to be trying to attract smart phone users with the ability to access the internet almost anywhere and instantly share you photos. But do you really need an expensive, heavy and complex large-sensor camera to post photos to Facebook and Twitter?
On the flip side I just can't see this camera being attractive to professional photographers or high end photography enthusiasts. While the inclusion of the electronic viewfinder is nice I found the all on-screen controls to be distracting and bothersome and the image quality was for the most part lackluster.

A note about durability. As I was finishing up the testing of this camera I bobbled the camera due to nerve damage and it took a spill. The height was not great, less than three feet, and the initial impact was on soil and grass. The lens came apart into numerous pieces. I was able to put the lens back together but it appears to have suffered internal damage and will not focus either automatically or manually. I accept that I caused this damage but I am very unimpressed with the durability of such an expensive camera.

I really can't recommend this camera. Three stars but barely.

A side note about Samsung's technical support that isn't reflected in my rating of this camera. Calling Samsung's support line was a complete nightmare. Audio quality was atrocious. At the end I was practically screaming to be heard. I spent close to an hour and a half on the phone speaking with seven different people. Each person I spoke to had to be told all my information, the camera's information and the reason for my call. Four times I was transferred to 'the proper department.' In the end I had a supervisor tell me, first that the camera did not exist and then, that it must be a UK version and I'd have to start all over and call their UK support line. I then contacted Samsung through their Facebook support page. It's been almost a week and they still haven't decided what to do about the camera/lens.

{Edit}
It took nearly a month of back and forth and arguing to get Samsung to agree my camera was a US version, it was under warranty and they would issue a repair ticket for it. It was shipped off at their expense, repaired surprisingly quickly and shipped back. The camera's now in working order. Only one thing marred the process. When they returned the camera and lens the put a cap on the rear of the lens (I'd shipped it with the lens attached) but only put a piece of what looked like a Post-It across the body opening. I found it odd they wouldn't properly cap the body to protect the sensor though on the whole the packing job, bubble wrapped and foam peanuts was well done. Kudos to their repair facility but I'm still very put off by the whole experience with their support people.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy NX EK-GN120ZKAXAR Galaxy Wireless Smart Android 4G Camera 20.3MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 4.8-Inch LCD with 18-55mm OIS Lens (Black)

Edifier P841 Comfortable Noise Isolating Over-Ear Headphones with Microphone and Volume Controls - White This is an extremely comfortable to wear set of lightweight over-ear headphones.

There's often a lot of noise in my house. A television on somewhere, dishes being done, and a nine year old that never stops talking. I like to use headphones as an escape. When headphones claim they are noise isolating I hold them to it. These headphones did not disappoint me. The nicely cushioned soft pleather covered ear cups adjust for angle to offer a secure fit that provides excellent insulation against ambient noise and are very comfortable to wear, even for extended periods of time.

I found that they could deliver the snap of live instruments, or the impression that I was at a club with the singer on the stage in front of me. When the music had stopped, there was still silence. I noticed that I enjoyed wearing them because of the peace and quiet, I didn't want to take them off actually. These headphones isolate out noise so well they made me consider wearing them when the kid's home just to be able to hear myself think.

The sound quality is crisp, great clarity not overpowering and provide a personal ambience. They offer a great balance and at no point was I confused when watching movies. They were even picking up the weighty and seismic bass from Jurassic Park that would imply a dinosaur was right behind me. The adjustable aluminum headphone band has a slight amount of padding beneath the pleather covered top part, but I wish it had just a little bit more to provide a bit more cushioning. Finally, the headphones are able to smoothly swivel flat for storage or packing although the cable is too long for me to want to use these for trips.

Overall I am incredibly happy with their quality, especially for the price. They're very comfortable, provide excellent noise isolation, and deliver very clean response with deep bass. I plan to enjoy using them and am pleased to recommend them on Amazon.

Retail sample provided at no cost by Edifier for my testing, evaluation, and review.

text_fidelity_a:
PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV If you read the product description carefully, you won't waste time (as I did) trying to use this PLAYSTATION 4 UNIVERSAL MEDIA REMOTE to navigate PS4 games (e.g., Journey, Minecraft). The PS4 remote uses Bluetooth to turn your PS4 on and off, and to control and navigate PS4 media (e.g., DVDs), but only controls PS4 media. The PS4 remote can also be programmed to turn your TV, Cable Box, and Audio Receiver on and off, and to control and navigate those devices (assuming they accept remote Bluetooth operation).

The PS4 remote performs the advertised functions very well, and I'm happy with it. The main thing I wanted was the PS4 on/off feature, so that I wouldn't have to fool with the skinny button on the PS4 box when I wanted to play a DVD. But I also wanted something that would make it easier to navigate DVDs. I'm not much of a gamer, and I find the game controllers awkward to use. With the PS4 remote, the forward, back, play, and arrow buttons work "normally" (like any TV remote).

NOTE THAT once the PS4 remote is paired, you will turn the playstation "on" by pressing the big PS4 button, but you will turn it "off" by navigating to the PS4's power settings (in the display). (The PS4 remote doesn't have a "sources" button for bringing up the output options on my Samsung Smart TV, so I still need a second remote for selecting the PS4 output.)

The Bluetooth pairing and setup for the PS4 remote is straightforward, but you need to follow the directions in the accompanying booklet "to the letter". You have to visit several locations in the PS4 settings to add the remote to the PS4 device list, and then complete the setup.

Programming the remote to turn on another device (TV, Cable Box, Amplifier, etc.) is exactly the same as programming any universal remote. You turn on the device you're programming, put the remote into learning mode, point it at the device, and wait for the remote to find, recognize, and turn off the device. If the remote doesn't recognize the device, you must perform the device code programming manually (lots of codes are listed in the instruction booklet). The PS4 remote recognized my TV without difficulty, but my sound bar required manual programming.

Once you've programmed the various other devices, you switch between those devices by pressing the little labeled buttons (PS4, TV, AMP, CBL). Which brings me to the only thing that I don't like about the PS4 remote--the buttons (especially the switching buttons) are quite small, because there are so many of them packed onto this rather narrow remote.
text_fidelity_b: PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV

text_fidelity_a:
Mount-It! Single Monitor Arm Mount | Desk Stand | Heavy Duty Full Motion Height Adjustable | Fits 19 21 24 27 29 30 in VESA 75 100 Compatible Computer Screen | C-Clamp Base | Holds up to 33 Lbs I purchased this specifically to mount a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465smh 24-Inch SuperClear MVA LED Monitor]]. It definitely holds the monitor - steady - in any position within this mount's range. Note that my monitor weighs in around 9.5 pounds, so factor that into your own needs.

Assembly is a snap. It comes with everything you need to mount the VESA adapter to your monitor, including washers and spacers. I had anticipated having to purchase bolts to fit, but that turned out to be unnecessary.

One of the things I love is the VESA bracket has slots that fit into horizontal posts. Those support the full weight of the monitor while you are installing the two adjustment bolts. In other words, assembling, mounting and adjusting this can be done by one person. My mount shipped with thumb style bolts and optional, heavier ones that you can use with the included hex wrench. Since my monitor was so light to begin with I used the thumb bolts, which hold the viewing angle in the narrow range of movement the VESA mount allows. Had my monitor been heavier I would have probably used the hex bolts, which are a lot beefier.

Bottom line: read some of the other reviews that discuss challenges that this mount has for heavier and larger monitors. However, if you have a 24" that is in the 10-12 pound range (or less) this is all the mount that you need. It's built like a tank, is a breeze to assemble, and holds lighter monitors absolutely rock steady.
text_fidelity_b: Mount-It! Single Monitor Arm Mount | Desk Stand | Heavy Duty Full Motion Height Adjustable | Fits 19 21 24 27 29 30 in VESA 75 100 Compatible Computer Screen | C-Clamp Base | Holds up to 33 Lbs

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser Momentum 3 Wireless - Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Alexa, Auto On/Off, Smart Pause Functionality and Smart Control App - White I ordered the 'New Sennheiser Momentum Wireless Noise Cancelling Headphones with Auto On/Off, Smart Pause Functionality and Smart Control App' to review. So far, and after almost a month of testing and playing with these amazing headphones, I am ready to share my thoughts.

First and foremost I must express that I am really disappointed in the case that Sennheiser has included with these "High End" Headphones. I mean come on Sennheiser. It seems pretty standard these days for higher end headphones to come with a nice clam-shell hard case. The case provided is a soft zipper pouch with little to no padding at all. I would not feel comfortable to stuff these into my backpack or even suitcase for that matter.

Now with that said, these headphones ARE solid. The stainless steel headband is sturdy and not fragile. The headphones themselves are of a very nice quality construction with real leather, both on the headband and ear pads. The physical buttons (which I tend to like much better than the new "touch" buttons on some of the others out there) are nice and solid and function perfectly.

The sound is absolutely AMAZING! I compared them to my wife's Bose QuietComfort 35 II headphones and honestly I love the sound signature on the Momentum's better. And as for the Noise Cancellation, I honestly can't tell much difference between the two. I do think the Bose do a slightly better job but for the sound quality you get out of the Momentum's, I'll stick with the Momentum's.

As for the weight and comfort compared to the Bose, the Bose are lighter but not necessarily more comfortable. The Momentum's just feel SOLID. The Bose feel nice but light and flimsy.

Other thoughts - Others complain about the "auto pause" feature on the Momentum's, but I personally love it. Others complain about the way you have to power these off by folding them up and personally, it doesn't bother me a bit. I would rather that then pressing a button and wondering if you pressed it correctly. This way, you KNOW they are off.

Battery life isn't the greatest compared to many others in this price range but for me it's just fine. I don't travel long distances and for the occasional 5-6 hour flights I rarely take, they will give me what I need. Plus with the much appreciated USB type C charging port, they will charge pretty fast.

Overall I LOVE everything about these, except for the soft flimsy case provided. Sound is fantastic! They are loud with rich thumping Bass, Nice clean Mids and wonderfully crisp Highs and for me the Sound Isolation works great.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser Momentum 3 Wireless - Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Alexa, Auto On/Off, Smart Pause Functionality and Smart Control App - White

text_fidelity_a:
Blink XT2 Outdoor/Indoor Smart Security Camera with cloud storage included, 2-way audio, 2-year battery life – 1 camera kit So I’m glad that I started with the single camera, because this would have been a huge disappointment. The system that allows remote viewing is unable to reboot itself when power is restored, so if your home loses power for some reason while you are not home, the sync Module does not automatically reconnect when the power comes back on. This ultimately renders the whole system useless since it can’t be relied upon when you are not home.

My original system, Zmodo does air reconnect so if my home loses power, the cameras reconnect as soon as they have power again. In fact the cameras were what alerted us to the return of power to our home during the 2016 fires in Napa. I will stick with them, despite the wiring issue. They are just more reliable.

The range from transmitting device is basic at best with them occasionally losing signal when phone is in pocket and I bend over and have my ear muffs on. I can get about 30' away from phone if there isn't any obstructions. They hold their charge well. They are pretty comfortable to wear especially since I typically have ear muffs over them. My only complaint really is the sound quality. Mids and highs are decent for this price range but there isn't really any lows. They are small devices so I'm not looking to thump but I'm not impressed compared to others I've worn.

GAOMON PD1560 15.6 Inches 8192 Levels Pen Display with Arm Stand 1920 x 1080 HD IPS Screen Drawing Tablet with 10 Shortcut Keys TL:DR - if you want a good tablet from a brand that cares about it's customers/users AND has good drivers/software in a 16" screen you can't go wrong with this device. Huion Kamvas Pros are good and all, but I've heard too many issues compared to this device with virtually none. Especially considering the total cost is around 350 - 375.

It's not perfect and pickier users like me may not like some of the workarounds, but for a first art tablet that is basically what I'd consider the best package and/or intro into digital art you can't go wrong.

The GAOMON PD1560 really surprised me with it's performance to price ratio. The device itself is light weight and comes with what I would dub as a starter bundle of accessories. Tablet, Stand, Glove, Nibs, Carrying case, etc. The line quality is also really amazing and when running my tests didn't notice any abnormal line wobble if any at all. Brad Coblow does a good review of it. Contratry to his review the quality isn't bad at all. If you've handled a computer monitor this tablet feels like it more or less. Drivers weren't an issue and the hot keys were fantastic.

The pen kept a great charge and felt nice to use along with the included artist glove (I got only a single two finger one). Drawing without the screen protector was a little squeaky at times, but had no issue in CS6 and CSP. The tablet stays nearly completely when you adjust the brightness/backlit to sub 65 degrees F. Luckily it doesn't change the looks all that much. There is a bit of parallax and calibration can take some time to get completely right but pen accuracy is top notch.

Screen quality is good and the cables are pretty rigid so no worries there. They actually connect by recessing into a slot rather than on the edge of the device.

Lastly is customer service. I really enjoyed GAOMON's customer service which I wish more companies would do.

There are a few caveats though. To get the pen the most accurate no matter where you point on the screen you need to understand where you touch the dot when calibrating. Next you need to hold the pen in the exact same orientation and way when you draw. That means holding the pen the exact same way with little deviation of that angle to get things to line up as well as say an iPad Pro. If you don't the distance when you calibrate really well is under say... 0.5mm or less. I am really stingy about this, but for someone who isn't this isn't a big thing to worry about.

Next are the hotkeys which act more like a macbook's butterfly keyboard in terms of presses. They press well and have very little travel almost like the old iphone home buttons. This may bother some, but didn't for me. I did need to place some tape with texture to understand where my buttons were without looking.

The screen protector I didn't install and I found it really annoying to even attempt to install. Then again I've written with fountain pens for 5 years now so am very used to buttery smooth pen work.
text_fidelity_b: GAOMON PD1560 15.6 Inches 8192 Levels Pen Display with Arm Stand 1920 x 1080 HD IPS Screen Drawing Tablet with 10 Shortcut Keys

Ultimate Ears TripleFi 10 Noise Isolating Earphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This was one of the last Ultimate Ears earbud lines before Logitech bought the company which resulted in an immediate drop in product quality and increase in product price. Yes, these are still wired headphones, but the sound fidelity is unmatched, and instead of complicated noise cancelling algorithms this simply employs noise isolation to block out ambient sound. These headphones have been out of production for some time, but for whatever reason you can still find them NIB from many vendors. They charge about a little more than what cut-rate vendors charged when they were new about 6 years ago, but they were way ahead of their time and frankly nothing on the market in this price range sounds even close to this good. Plus, these original UE headphones (I don't evangelize anything UE after Logitech bought them) have a lot of great design features. The earbud units are modular, so if you ever destroy the leads, you can always replace them for $10. Also, the standard leads these ship with do NOT have the mic and volume/start-stop control on the leads, but you can buy them in various levels of quality for about $20-60 aftermarket and swap them out. It's money well spent if you want to make calls on them. Also, the lead up to 6" from each bud is cased in memory metal so they can be bent to shape and hold in place to are a comfy fit on he outside of your ears- great idea.

All around the best earbud headphones for the money, if you can find them!
text_fidelity_b: Ultimate Ears TripleFi 10 Noise Isolating Earphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Tribit Bluetooth Speaker, XSound Go Speaker with 16W Loud Sound & Deeper Bass, 24H Playtime, IPX7 Waterproof, Bluetooth 5.0 TWS Pairing Portable Wireless Speaker for Home, Outdoor (Upgraded) In full disclosure, I must admit that I miss my Bose Bluetooth speaker. Their acoustics are impeccable. The "Tribit XSound Go Bluetooth Speakers" only cost a fraction of my Bose speaker. I first purchased the "DOSS Touch Wireless Bluetooth" which is in the same price range; I returned that product because it lacked bass and was unimpressive overall. The Tribit, however, has plenty of bass for such a small speaker. Ironically, the problem that I have is the treble! I think it is an inherent problem with smaller speakers and not this particular device. I have installed an equalizer on my computer which mitigates some of the problems and makes the speaker sound very acceptable.

The pros:
• The speaker is loud! It is perfect for a jam session in your bedroom. I'm not sure it is suitable for large or multi rooms.
• The quality is good, and the speaker looks like a million bucks.
• It has an excellent microphone that works well with phone calls and even to interact with Siri or Cortana.
• The Play button allows one to answer, reject or end a call. It also can play or pause a song. Finally, it allows you to skip a music track forward or backward.

The cons:
• While the bass is fairly impressive, the treble is slightly overriding.
• The battery does not nearly last for 24 hours if you like to blast music as I do
• The speaker can only be paired to one device at a time. If you are listening to music on the computer and the phone tries to connect, the speaker will sometimes disconnect from all devices. The speaker does have an av input one could connect to the computer but obviously, the speaker would no longer be completely portable. This could be a deal breaker for many.

After comparing this speaker with others in its price range, I realize that this speaker has such poor sound quality that I could never recommend it to anyone.
text_fidelity_b: Tribit Bluetooth Speaker, XSound Go Speaker with 16W Loud Sound & Deeper Bass, 24H Playtime, IPX7 Waterproof, Bluetooth 5.0 TWS Pairing Portable Wireless Speaker for Home, Outdoor (Upgraded)

10.1" Car DVD Player with Free Wireless Headphone Support HDMI Input, Sync Screen, AV in & Out, Last Memory, USB SD - NAVISKAUTO If you are looking for a portable DVD player that has intuitive controls, a remote control and a case to hold the DVD player so you can view the screen while seated in the back of a vehicle, this is a good choice. The screen swivels around so you can fold this in half "backwards" so only the screen is showing. This is helpful when using the case for use in a vehicle.

Compared to my regular TV this is an enhanced viewing experience. I found this to be a better visual experience. All the colors were vivid and almost velvety. Whether I am watching a favorite movie or a nature DVD, the colors are fantastic. Greens and yellows are super crisp and water looks totally glossy. I can't emphasize enough how beautiful the colors are on the screen.

I found many uses for this DVD player. It literally became my entertainment companion for two days while I tried out every feature. What I loved best was playing my virtual fireplace DVD with a beach fire and ocean waves. The stereo sound on this is excellent, I felt I was really at the beach which made me happy.

The remote control works very well and allows you to do things like turn the subtitles on or off. The audio controls let you choose between various options. You can stop or pause the movie you are watching either from the controls on the DVD player or by using the remote control.

This DVD player also has a screen saver that comes up when you put it on pause or don't turn the screen off. There is a button that says TFT ON/OFF that turns the screen off when you only want to listen to the sound. I found this played CDs too so that made me very happy. You can listen with the stereo speakers or use headphones.

If you are looking to view widescreen movies, this works for that too.

This is perfect to take with you when traveling. The only caution is not to use it for yourself if you are driving. It does have a cigarette charger that will work in cars and RVs.

The only thing I do when taking out a CD or DVD is to turn the DVD player off completely.

Some other uses I found for this DVD player was to play relaxing DVDs before bed to calm the mind. I also watched an underwater DVD with fish swimming by. This DVD player allows you to have entertainment wherever you are. The battery lasts about 4-5 hours, but if it starts to run out you can just plug the unit in and continue watching.

The only thing I noticed that was different than a regular DVD player was when you are halfway through a movie, put it on pause instead of taking out the DVD. This does not seem to have any memory of where you left off so when you put the DVD back in it just starts from the beginning again. This is not a big issue if you just hit the pause button.

I'm very happy with this DVD player and it is fun to go into your own little movie world. This is handy to have when someone else is using the computer or main TV. You can watch movies anywhere you want. I use this mostly when sitting in bed.

~The Rebecca Review

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic Bryker Convertible Backpack (BRYBP114) I travel quite a bit and many of the trips I take are short in duration- often only two or three nights. I don’t need a lot of luggage space for these short trips and I like taking backpacks because I can often avoid carry- on and baggage fees if my backpack can fit under my seat. This desire for economical travel led me to get the Case Logic BRYBPR116 Bryker Backpack Roller.

With this Case Logic Backpack, you get a two-in-one backpack and piece of luggage well suited for travel or business. The wheels make it perfect for traversing an airport and with the added straps, you can carry it on your back, like a traditional backpack. There is an outside pocket where you can tuck the straps so they are not hanging out, flopping around when you don’t need them. And the handle can be completely pushed inside the backpack and sealed off with a zipper so that no one sees it. I like these qualities because it means I can make this look like a backpack when I want it to and I can make it look more like a piece of luggage when I want it to.

Inside the backpack, there is a separate compartment for a laptop and I like that you can unsnap this if you like, making for a larger interior space that is just right for stuffing your two- day supply of clothing and personal items. Like I said, my primary usage with this backpack is for travel and I usually don’t take my laptop with me when I’m on a two- day trip, so I would rather have the open space, to make it more like a piece of luggage.

There is one thing to keep in mind if you take this backpack on a plane, and that is the size of pack makes it only barely able to fit under your seat. It will stick out some, so be prepared to have a snug space where your feet normally go. And unlike other backpacks, it’s too rigid- thanks to the handle- to make it collapsible and flexible. To save having to pay carry- on fees on certain airlines, I am willing to place it under the airline seat in front of me regardless, even if it does stick out some. If your flying on an airline that doesn’t charge extra for carry-ons, then this won’t be an issue since you can easily place the backpack in the overhead, which is what I recommend doing. For everyone else, just bear in mind that the length of the backpack makes it a challenge to fit under a seat.

I have a wide assortment of backpacks and luggage in my home to accommodate different needs. This Case Logic rolling backpack is a nice addition to my collection and I like that it performs a dual role. It has suited me well so far and it makes a good choice of luggage/backpack for business people and others who are constantly on the go for short spans of time.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic Bryker Convertible Backpack (BRYBP114)

text_fidelity_a:
Zinwell ZAT-970A Digital to Analog TV Converter Box (for Antenna Use) We needed to save some money, and I'd heard that Over The Air broadcasts included channels you wouldn't otherwise get. My Dish TV account provided local channels and a whole bunch of channels I didn't use; but the OTA feature really helps!

I paired the Zinwell digital / analog converter box (highly rated, outstanding Amazon price) with the Radio Shack Antennacraft® HDX1000 Amplified HDTV Antenna (also highly rated). You should know one thing -- the mast size for the Dish TV is larger than the mast size for the Antennacraft antenna, so you can't just remove the Dish and replace it with the Antennacraft on the same mast. But it is an easy install.

As a trial, before going up to the roof (2 story house), I set the Antennacraft in the downstairs window that has a view to the southwest (the direction our local TV stations broadcast from). Without the Zinwell, you're limited to the low power analog stations (mostly Spanish language, a few home shopping stations). I think I got about 6 stations. Then I plugged in the Zinwell in line between the antenna and the TV (after disconnecting the Dish TV feed), did a scan, and had 20 channels. Repeated the process upstairs (remember, we have a 2 story) and had 22 channels!! All the local tv stations (NBC, ABC, CW, ION, PBS, etc.) that broadcast digitally came through great!! Unfortunately, it started raining :( so after the rain stopped, I only got as far as getting the mast installed outdoors before it got too dark. It won't take long to finish.

Only one Zinwell related item: You're supposed to be able to choose the feed from the Zinwell to the TV to be either Coax or the Composite (yellow video, red and white audio). I couldn't get the composite to work in setup, but the coax worked just fine. Haven't had a chance to see if, once programmed, the composite would work, or if for some reason I hooked it up to my tv incorrectly (hard to imagine), but ... since the coax works so well, and video and audio quality are great, I'm money ahead and not complaining!!

So when do I break even? $80 antenna plus 2 $40 boxes = $160; Dish TV was costing me about $55/month (yeah, once you've been a subscriber for a while, there's essentially no customer retention policy, so, good by Dish!! -- and that's probably true for Directv and Comcast, too). So after 3 months, essentially at the start of January, I'm home free!! Thanks, Amazon, you're helping me save money, and that's really great!!

NOTE: I only ordered one Zinwell to test out things, now I've ordered a second for our other TV (didn't want to put too much at risk if it didn't work, but it works great!).

NOTE 2: The gov't coupon program is long dead, no hope of getting $40 off on one, just be glad if you waited that these things are as reasonably priced as they are.
text_fidelity_b: Zinwell ZAT-970A Digital to Analog TV Converter Box (for Antenna Use)

text_fidelity_a:
Tiffen 82VND 82 Millimeter Variable ND Filter Shooting video outdoors with a DSLR requires, obviously, proper exposure. When shooting at 24 (23.978) frames per second, the normal shutter speed should be 1/50th of a second (1/60 at 29.97 fps). If the camera is set at the lowest ISO rating of 100, in bright daylight the f/stop would be around f/22. If you want to operate at wider aperture to achieve shallow depth of field, you need to cut the light.

This variable density filter allows such an adjustment. The problem is that it cuts the light by rotating two polarizing filters against each other. Polarizers can be tricky and, by design, modify the quality of light. Thus it may act unexpectedly.

One downside is that the front of the filter is not threaded and my 77mm model is a larger diameter than the 70-200mm Nikon zoom it fits on. So now the bayonet lens hood won't fit. Now I'm outdoors with a filter on the lens and no hood to block flare. There aren't any hoods that naturally fit the filter so you need to tape a hood to the outer ring or use a matte box.
text_fidelity_b: Tiffen 82VND 82 Millimeter Variable ND Filter

text_fidelity_a:
Roku N1100 HD Media Player (Old Model) I've been researching ways to increase my cable channel happiness and reduce the costs. My research started a while ago, but a Cosumerist post about subscriber fees really got my goat. Look at all the junk channels that we are forced to pay for. I could care less about any sports channel or 90% of everything else. It is my opinion that we should be able to choose extra channels separately after we hook up with basic cable. You'll also notice that BH charges extra for a special HD tier. Sure it's only $6 a month, but geez, look how much markup there is. Anyways, you get the idea. I don't have any issues with BH. They've served me well for a few years. But I need more of what I want. Not what BH thinks I want.

So, I dropped down to basic cable and purchased a Roku HD unit. Set-up was a snap. I used HDMI for the TV and stream with a N router.

OMFG! This thing is amazing! In short, it streams unlimited Netflix offerings to your TV. The cheapest Netflix subscription ($9) is all you need. Plus it streams Amazon Video On Demand, and a bunch of internet channels. You can stream wirelessly or hard wire with an ethernet cable.

Can you tell I'm excited? Anytime I can boost my entertainment for less dollars is always a good day. The Roku will pay for itself in 2 months after switching to basic. And its HD!

Sigh...I must go.

I've been watching the original Dr. Who from the 60's.
text_fidelity_b: Roku N1100 HD Media Player (Old Model)

text_fidelity_a:
Jaybird X2 Sport Wireless Bluetooth Headphones - Midnight Black Finally seem to have found a pair of bluetooth headphones with acceptable connection performance. I was begining to think that it was too much to ask to be able to put my phone in my pocket and still be connected. Or to walk more than a few feet away from my phone and still stay connected. These ace those tests. Connectivity is not perfect but I am willing to accept that as it's bluetooth. I do get the occasional drop for no apparent reason but it is not often enough to be a huge negative.
They come packaged really nicely. So nicely you almost feel obligated to go slow and enjoy the experience.
You have to chose between the silicone or foam ear bud tips. The silicone feels softer and goes in and out easier. The foam will give you a more secure fit and sound isolation. I went with the foam and they do a fairly good job of keeping the outside world out. They are by no means 100 percent effective though.
I used the medium foam tips as well as the ear wings and find the comfort pretty good and the fit very secure. Wearing them for a couple hours was not an issue and I had no discomfort.
I cannot comment on their ability to transmit music as I use them for podcasts. Sound quality was fine for speech.
These have come down in price so much lately that I think they are a no brainer compared to the competition.
I dropped them a star due to the occasional random connection failure but overall I am very pleased with them.
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird X2 Sport Wireless Bluetooth Headphones - Midnight Black

But, with the better speeds now available with Cox, it was time to move to a DOCSIS 3.1 modem.

Installation was simple with the only struggle being getting the modem registered with Cox. That's a process that I can't do on my own in my service area -- I have to call in to Cox and provide them with the model number, serial number and MAC address info. Once they managed to record it correctly, it was a simple process to swap out the old modem for the new.

I like the new design of the indicator lights. It's still bright, but not the shining beacon in the night style of older Arris modems. The heat while operating is not bad, but it's still sufficiently warm that it's best to keep the modem in the open to allow for good air circulation.

So far so good. I'll update the review down the road should reliability be an issue. At present, a 5 star product.

The output for the USB ports is 5V, 3A Max.

The USB ports glow blue whether you use them or not. The blue light is bright during the day and night, and can be seen even when there is a cable plugged into a port. I like and don’t like the illumination. It’s helpful at night if I need to plug something in, but then, the light is very bright in a dark room.

The cube doesn’t block the outlet below it, which I also like. If plugged into the bottom outlet on a normal wall socket, it will block the top outlet.

I like the small size, it’s great for keeping in your bag in case you need a bunch of outlets. But it’s also functional at home, and has replaced one of my bulky power strips.

The surge protector is made in China.

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Basics SDHC Class 4 16GB Secure Digital Card the plus to this card is obvious--it has a large capacity.  The con is that it is a little slow in picture-taking.  Depending on what you're looking for, you may be happy or dissatisfied. I used it in a Kodak flip-style camcorder/still picture taker and I liked the fact that I didn't have to worry about filling up the card.  I recorded at 720 and it did fine in the recording and in the downloading of the video--I really didn't notice any speed issues.  Picture-taking was a different story; there was a noticeable lag in taking still photos. I wouldn't dismiss this card for that reason, however, unless a difference of a second or so will matter to you.  Most of my still picture taking on vacation is done with a larger point and shoot Canon IS, so the lag time with the little camera didn't matter much to me as I either used it mostly for video as mentioned or took stills of landscape or posed photos.  To be honest, I prefer not to use such a large capacity card for photos anyway as I have a fear of something going wrong with the card and losing hundreds of photos as opposed to a few videos.  So I'm happy to keep this in the little compact video camera and snap the occasional slow photo. I wouldn't put it in my Canon for the above reason and also because the photos I take with that I'd be more concerned about the sluggish picture-taking.  Be selective about how you use it, and I think you'll be more than satisfied
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics SDHC Class 4 16GB Secure Digital Card

To say I am a music lover is definitely an understatement. The product information on these particular earpieces really stressed the music features  instead of the phone features so I just had to have them. These are quite amazing! Everything in the product description is accurate and honest. I paired these with my Ipad first or should I say the set did. All I did was open the case. They paired immediately. You can use these together or just one. Once just one is taking out then the other will disconnect on its own. You want it back just take it out of the case and it will pair with the other piece again on its own. The sound quality is definitely well balanced between sound and comfort. The bass and treble are really well tuned. You will not hear anything else when wearing both pieces not matter how high or low the volume is. I got 12 hours of straight playtime on one charge and exactly 10 full charges with the charging case. There is only one button on these which is the only thing I don't like because I always have such a hard time pushing it in just the right way for each function but I think that's just a personal preference kind of thing. I also used these with my Iphone 8 plus and again it paired automatically and again with my HP laptop. All the same across all my devices without any effort at all, that's a first. The phone calls also did pretty amazing. No drops, lags or glitches of any kind. The sound was just as great as the music. I could hear clearly with the caller and there was absolutely no outside sounds interfering and the caller could hear me clearly as well. The case is so compact and stored easily in my bag. The pieces are extremely comfortable. I sleep in mine so that I can listen and no one will be bothered by it. This is the first pair that are this small to actually stay in my ears overnight. So, this was a lot of first for just one Bluetooth. I still can't believe it myself but it definitely is. I have already suggested these to a few family members. They are that great. Oh, I did wear these in the shower and they are waterproof. You just can't immerse them in water like swimming.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) My husband and I just purchased a Fire yesterday and I'm absolutely in love with it. We've been drooling over it for quite some time, going to "visit" it everytime we went to Target. At first when we found out that it didn't have the e-ink technology it dampened our feelings towards it for a second or two but then we found out all the other cool stuff it can do - videos, magazines and kid books IN COLOR and suddenly we realized that maybe this could be our answer to our computer problems. We own a serious lemon of a laptop and can't afford a new one at the moment but the Kindle Fire is perfect for what we need - checking e-mail, netflix, browsing, etc... so that is the primary purpose we bought it for. Here is a quick list of the good and bad I've noticed:

Bad:
-Even though I knew it was a 7" screen and I've seen the floor models it still kind of shocked me when we took it out of the box. but, so far it hasn't really been an issue - but if you have been looking at i-pads and and considering the Fire instead just realize that it is smaller.

Good:
-No Set up process - the most I did to start using the Fire was enter my amazon user name and password so it could link the device to my account
-Beautiful display. The color is crisp and there is no fuzziness - I am noticing now how fuzzy my work devices are now!
-Quick! Amazon Silk and the Dual Core Processor in the Fire result in an incredibly quick browsing experience, you flash from one screen to another with no loading time
-Cloud Storage - I love that I can store all of my amazon purchased material FREE on the cloud - no more running out of memory on a device. I purchase all of my ebooks and such from Amazon, but if someone else gets it from another source they can still purchase additional storage
-Easy to navigate. We aren't what you could call tech savy people, and this was the first Kindle my husband has ever touched but neither of us has had trouble navigating it.
-full color magazines and kid books - not that I'm going to completely drop my glossies but it will be nice to have some on the Fire when I'm on the go, I like to travel lite. We're especially excited about the children's books our two young daughters (both under 5) like to have me read from my other Kindle to them but they still need pictures and unfortunately on my other device the layout for these books wasn't great. The layout on the fire however, is gorgeous and I can't wait to show the girls
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

It feels as solid as my name-brand binoculars, not like cheap plastic like some off-brands.

I’ve had binocular clips for phone cameras before this one, but this is the most sturdy design I’ve seen. I love it! I get very sick from shaking which meant for a long time monoculars were out of the question as well as some binoculars. It’s difficult to follow fast moving birds, but for ones that are sitting still this is an excellent option! I have a Pixel 6 Pro and had no problems hooking it up to the monoscope and giving it a whirl.

The tripod included is alright, it’s solid enough and when tightened well it works great, I found it a little fiddly to tighten and accidentally knocked off one of the knobs! It can hold the monoscope and my phone just fine despite the imbalance, and the universal mount means you can always use your tripod of choice.

We took some pictures from the cliffs near where we live, it’s pretty powerful. I also took a photo of the moon, you could see the pits and craters. It can be difficult to aim, especially at night but it seems to take practice–I didn’t use the tripod for that shot, which would have made it clearer. The woodchuck is with a tripod and fully zoomed.

What made me interested was the carrying case, which would fit perfectly into a hiking day-bag. My husband and I love to bird and this would be great for spotting owls at dusk! It’s stronger than my standard binoculars.

Donner Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.2 Earphones with 4 Mic Clear Calls, 12mm Drivers, App for Custom EQ, 32H Playtime, Fast Charging, Transparency - Dobuds ONE, Blue Budget-priced earbuds are complicated to review because, in my experience, all $200 earbuds sound significantly better than all $50 earbuds, but there is still a lot of demand for value-priced "good enough" products. I do own a couple of $200 earbuds and they do sound noticeably richer and clearer than these $40 earbuds. However, when I'm out jogging or traveling (eg airplane or train) or listening to voice podcasts, having the absolute best sound quality isn't really important to me. In those situations, features are more important to me, like active noise cancellation, equalization, good volume, good battery life, and easy access to the features. I'd rather use cheap earbuds that I don't mind losing somewhere along the way.

These earbuds have average quality sound for the $40 price. Where these Donner earbuds beat the competition is the features. I've never owned $40 earbuds with app control before. The user manual has a QR code to let you download the app. The QR code did not work, but I did find the "Donner Control" app in the Google Play app store and the app works fine on my Android phone. The app lets me pick from pre-programmed equalization settings or design my own. Adjusting the equalization for different types of music makes a significant difference in audio clarity. The app also lets me choose from 3 active noise cancellation modes. These features don't work as well as in $200 earbuds, but these are $40 earbuds and most $40 earbuds don't have any of these features or any app at all. You can control some of these features with the confusing set of triple-tap commands on the earbuds, but I can never remember those and would rather just tap the picture in the app.

The app also lets you download firmware updates from Donner. None was available when I checked, but this could be a great way for them to refine the features of the earbuds or even add new features. They ask you to give them your email address and create an account when you open the app, but I did not and the core features of the app still work OK.

Battery life for these earbuds is good for this price range (6 to 8 hours, depending on whether or not you use ANC). As with most budget-priced wireless earbuds, maximum volume is OK but not great. Bass is above average for the $40 price. Static noise is very low. The Bluetooth connection has been very stable for me, even when I'm 30 feet away from my phone or in a different room in the house.

I can't give these earbuds 5 stars because I can easily buy better sound quality with more money, but these are solid 4 stars for value at the current $40 price.
